chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Tharid is the food of the Arabs.

key_terms.الثَّرِيدُ: Al-Tharid, a traditional dish consisting of bread soaked in meat broth and fat.
key_terms.الْعَرَبِ: The Arabs, referring to the Arab people or their cultural identity.

ai.seo_question: What is Al-Tharid and why is it significant in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) identifies Al-Tharid as the quintessential food of the Arabs, a designation that underscores its historical significance as a staple dish in the Arabian Peninsula. This narration reflects the cultural culinary norms of the time, which the Imams acknowledged and often utilized as a benchmark for describing other foods or virtues in hadith literature.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Al-Sareyd is the food of the Arabs’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Tharid is the food of Arabs.’”
